mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the Fed's higher policy rate compresses discount rates, reducing the present value of future equity cash flows and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in this regime are not statistically lower than in pre-hike periods (p > 0.05 t-test), or FEDFUNDS MA(3) never exceeds 4.5% in the observed window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the CPIAUCSL inflation index below 2.0% for three consecutive months signals disinflation, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady and allowing equity discount rates to normalize, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during this condition are not statistically higher than during persistent inflation (>2.0%) periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) above 135,000 monthly coincides with rising hiring momentum that boosts consumer demand, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in this regime are not statistically positive vs. the prior month's average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (real GDP growth) exceeds 3% in the quarter ending prior to the decision date, the acceleration of business investment and consumer confidence drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during this signal are not significantly higher than during flat or negative GDP growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below 98.0 for two consecutive months indicates softening supply-side capacity, which amplifies demand imbalances and tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during this condition are not statistically higher than during robust production periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls by more than 0.3 percentage points in three months, the labor market strengthens, reducing risk premia and pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during this regime are not statistically positive vs. prior high-unemployment periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales) below 900 and 410 million dollars, respectively, for two consecutive months indicate weakening housing and consumer demand, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 900 AND RSAFS < 410 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during this dual weakness are not statistically lower than during normal conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in FEDFUNDS above 1.5% for three consecutive months in a non-inflationary regime is interpreted as persistent tightening, which raises real discount rates and typically yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 1.5% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 2.0
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during this regime are not statistically lower than during similar periods with FEDFUNDS ≤ 1.5% (p > 0.05).
